title: Kth Largest With a Bounded Min-Heap
statement:
Sorting the whole array to find one element is more work than the
question actually needs: a `PriorityQueue` kept at size `k` -- evicting
its smallest element every time a new one would push it over that size --
ends up holding exactly the `k` largest elements seen, with the smallest
of *those* sitting right at the top. That smallest-of-the-k-largest is,
by definition, the k-th largest overall.

## Your function

```
public static int kthLargest(int[] values, int k);
```

`k` is always between `1` and `values.length` (inclusive) -- `k == 1`
asks for the maximum, `k == values.length` asks for the minimum. Return
the k-th largest element of `values`, counting duplicates as separate
elements (`{5, 5}` with `k = 2` is `5`, not "no second-largest exists").

## Watch out

- **`new PriorityQueue<Integer>()` is a *min*-heap by default** --
  `poll()` removes the smallest element, not the largest. That is exactly
  what this approach wants: keeping the heap capped at size `k` and
  evicting the smallest whenever it grows past that means the heap always
  holds the `k` largest elements encountered so far, and evicting the
  smallest of *those* is precisely how a new, larger element is allowed
  to displace the weakest current member of the top-`k`.
- **Evict only when the size *exceeds* `k`, i.e. `size() > k`, not
  `size() >= k`.** The second version starts evicting one element too
  early -- while the heap is still being filled up to its intended size --
  and the heap never actually settles at holding `k` elements at all.
- **`peek()`, not `poll()`, once the heap holds the `k` largest values.**
  `peek()` reads the minimum without removing it, which is what you want
  to report as the answer; `poll()` would remove it too, and iterating
  the `PriorityQueue` directly (or converting it to a list) does *not*
  give elements in sorted order at all -- only repeated `poll()` calls do,
  because the internal array is heap-ordered, not fully sorted.

tests.name: every element is the same value
